item.title: MJR Morning Brief — November 12, 2026
item.description:
From Media Jobs Report, here's what's happening across the media industry.
Stingray Group reports a strong second quarter, with revenue jumping 51 percent to 171 million Canadian dollars. Adjusted earnings climbed nearly 48 percent, fueled by its TuneIn acquisition and growing FAST channel business. Stingray's Radio division also posted gains in revenue and earnings. Read the full financial report at Media Jobs Report dot com.
Elsewhere in public broadcasting,
NPR has welcomed nine new and returning members to its Board of Directors, including public media executives from across the country. Jo Lambert was reelected Board Chair, while R.C. McBride was named Vice Chair. The appointments bring additional leadership experience and geographic representation to NPR's 23-member governing board.
In television news,
Jennifer Lopez is bringing her Las Vegas residency to television on Thanksgiving. The JLO Show: Live in Las Vegas premieres November 26 on CBS and Paramount+, featuring her biggest hits, a full orchestra and 16 dancers. An extended version will stream exclusively on Paramount+.
Turning to radio,
Cumulus Media’s 98.1 The Max in Memphis has raised a record $1.14 million for Ronald McDonald House Charities of Memphis. The eight-hour radiothon marked the third consecutive year the station has topped $1 million. Donations will help provide housing, meals and support for families with children receiving medical care.
In podcasting news,
OutKast legend Big Boi is keeping it in the family with a new iHeartPodcasts series. “Bloodlines & Basslines” features Big Boi and his sons, Bamboo and Cross Patton, sharing candid conversations about music, fatherhood, family and life. The podcast premieres November 11, with three new 10-minute episodes each week.
Turning to music,
Borchetta Entertainment Group has named Abby Miller Head of Artist Development. Miller brings nearly a decade of experience in artist management, digital strategy and A&R, including previous roles at Black River Entertainment and The Digital Dept. She'll work with artists including Carly Pearce, Molly Tuttle and The Band Perry.
In public media news,
Veteran media executive Sarah van Mosel has joined New Hampshire Public Radio as Chief Growth Officer. The move reunites her with President and CEO Jim Schachter, a former colleague at New York Public Radio. Van Mosel brings more than two decades of experience, including leadership roles at iHeartMedia, SiriusXM and Stitcher.
And finally,
The E.W. Scripps Company has promoted Christina Hartman to Chief Technology Officer. Hartman will oversee the company’s digital development, broadcast technology, cybersecurity and artificial intelligence initiatives. She previously led emerging technology operations and held several leadership roles at Scripps News.
Stay current with more media news, the latest jobs and free industry tools at MediaJobsReport.com.
